text_blocks.snippet: Bipolar disorder has a strong genetic component, meaning a family history of the condition increases the likelihood of developing it. While there's no single "bipolar gene," research indicates that multiple genes, in combination with environmental factors, play a role. Having a first-degree relative with bipolar disorder significantly elevates the risk, but it's not a guarantee that someone will develop the condition.
Key aspects of the genetic predisposition to bipolar disorder:

list.title: Family history:
list.snippet: If a first-degree relative (parent or sibling) has bipolar disorder, the risk of developing the condition increases to 15-30%. If both parents have it, the risk can be as high as 50-75%.
